title: Smooth source restriction identifies the sliced nearby-cycle comparison
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be finite-type morphisms, put $f=gh$, and suppose $h$ smooth on an open subscheme $W\subset X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\Lambda$ be finite killed by an integer invertible on $S$, and $M$ a finite $\Lambda$-module; write $\underline M$ for its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every base change $T\to S$, geometric specialization $b_T\to a_T$ over $b\to a$, and geometric $x_T\in W_{a_T}$ with image $y_T\in Y_{a_T}$, the ordinary comparison cones satisfy
$$C^f_T(\underline M)_{x_T}\simeq C^g_T(\underline M)_{y_T}.$$
Here $C$ denotes the sliced comparison cone on a geometric special fibre, as in [lem-trf-nearby-proper-source-exchange]; this assertion does not require $h$ proper. The isomorphism is compatible with further base changes. Also for every scheme $S$, $R\Psi_{1_S}\underline M\simeq p_2^*\underline M$, compatibly with arbitrary base change, so $(1_S,\underline M)$ is $\Psi$-good [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].

source.place: Lemma 4.2 and its truncated universal variant, pp. 11--12; identity case at the beginning of §4. Source proves this from strict-local smooth acyclicity. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Put $A=S_{(a)}$ and let $B\to A$ be the generization map used in the sliced $i_a^*Rj_{b,*}$ construction. Thus $B=S_{(b)}$ for a strict-local slice (or $B=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_b$ for its geometric-point slice). Write $Z_A=Z\times_S A$, $Z_B=Z_A\times_A B$, $j_Z:Z_B\to Z_A$, and $i_Z:Z_a\to Z_A$, for $Z=X,Y,W$. These are precisely the sliced functors and cones specified in lem-trf-nearby-proper-source-exchange; only its definition of $C$, not its proper-exchange assertion, is used. The same notation with primes applies over $T$. Each $j_Z$ is qcqs: $B\to A$ is a map between affine schemes, hence on a principal affine open its inverse image is principal affine, and its diagonal is the closed affine immersion given by the surjective multiplication map $\mathcal O(B)\otimes_{\mathcal O(A)}\mathcal O(B)\to\mathcal O(B)$; qcqs is preserved by base change. The restrictions $h_A:W_A\to Y_A$ and $h_T:W_T\to Y_T$ are smooth. Indeed finite presentations base change by tensoring their presentations, and an infinitesimal lifting problem for the base change is solved by lifting the map to $W$ and pairing it with the already given map to the new base. The same argument applies to every further base change. Finally, $\underline M$ is bounded constructible: it is finite locally constant on the single stratum which is the whole scheme, in degree zero. Its pullbacks are again the same constant sheaf.

proof.text:
Apply sbc-thm-bounded-derived-smooth-base-change with smooth map $h_A:W_A\to Y_A$ and qcqs map $j_Y:Y_B\to Y_A$. The constant finite $\Lambda$-module $\underline M$ on $Y_B$ satisfies its coefficient and constructibility hypotheses by step 1; the annihilating integer remains invertible after all these pullbacks. The ordinary exchange is therefore an isomorphism
$$h_A^*Rj_{Y,*}\underline M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{W,*}\underline M.$$
Pulling back by $i_W$, using $h_Ai_W=i_Yh_a$, gives
$$\alpha:h_a^*\Psi^g_{a,b}\underline M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi^{f|_W}_{a,b}\underline M.$$
Over $T$ the identical argument gives $\alpha_T:h_{a_T}^*\Psi^{g_T}_{a_T,b_T}\underline M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi^{f_T|_{W_T}}_{a_T,b_T}\underline M$. Here exact module inverse image is the termwise inverse image. The restriction from $X$ to $W$ in these formulas does not alter the stalk at the point in question: etale localization exchange applied to the open immersion $W_A\to X_A$ identifies $(Rj_{X,*}\underline M)|_{W_A}$ with $Rj_{W,*}\underline M$. The cited forget-coefficients exchange identifies this statement for modules with the abelian version of etale localization. The same holds over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change; Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian. Application: Orgogozo, Lemma 4.2 proof, printed p. 12, and identity case at beginning of section 4, printed p. 11 (author PDF read online; archival PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Let $u_Y:Y_{a_T}\to Y_a$ and $u_W:W_{a_T}\to W_a$. Write $\beta_g$ and $\beta_W$ for the ordinary sliced comparisons over $T$. The square with top row $h_{a_T}^*u_Y^*\Psi^g\underline M\to h_{a_T}^*\Psi^{g_T}\underline M$, bottom row $u_W^*\Psi^{f|_W}\underline M\to\Psi^{f_T|_{W_T}}\underline M$, and vertical maps $u_W^*\alpha$, $\alpha_T$, commutes. Here the top arrow is $h_{a_T}^*\beta_g$ and the bottom one is $\beta_W$, with the canonical inverse-image composition identifications understood. To check the arrows, before restricting by $i_W$ transpose each exchange under the appropriate $j^*\dashv Rj_*$: its transpose is the inverse-image square identification followed by the pullback of the $j$-counit, exactly the formula in sbc-def-base-change-map. Pasting first the source square then the base square, or first the base square then the source square, gives the same inverse-image square. Mate pasting (clauses 1 and 2) consequently gives the same comparison. The slice squares need not be cartesian; only the counit formula of def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles for a commutative square is used. The same pasting also compares the restriction from $X$ to $W$ with the comparisons: the restriction isomorphisms $\rho:(\Psi^f\underline M)|_{W_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi^{f|_W}\underline M$ and $\rho_T$ of step 2 are, by the statement of lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-exchange, the exchange morphisms of the cartesian squares $W_B\to X_B$ over $W_A\to X_A$ (followed by $i_W^*$), with the same transposed form. Pasting it with the base square in either order, mate pasting gives $\rho_T\circ(\beta_f|_{W_{a_T}})=\beta_W\circ u_W^*\rho$. Hence $C^f_T(\underline M)|_{W_{a_T}}\simeq C^{f|_W}_T(\underline M)$, by the cone transport of step 4. Repeating the pasting for $T'\to T\to S$ proves compatibility of the square with every further base change.

proof.text:
Take cones of the comparison square of step 3, obtaining
$$h_{a_T}^*C^g_T(\underline M)\simeq C^{f|_W}_T(\underline M).$$
This is a formal consequence of an isomorphism of arrows: transport a cone triangle of the top arrow along the two vertical isomorphisms; TR1 makes the transported triangle a cone triangle of the bottom arrow. Equivalently, on compatible complex representatives use $C(u)^r=L^r\oplus K^{r+1}$ and its displayed matrix differential from def-weil-abstract-derived-category. Exact inverse image commutes with this finite-sum construction, so this choice of cone comparison respects the pastings in step 3. Now take the geometric stalk at $x_T$. By definition of inverse image along the composite geometric point, $(h_{a_T}^*C^g_T)_{x_T}=(C^g_T)_{y_T}$. The restriction compatibility at the end of step 3, with the same transport of cone triangles, identifies the other stalk with $(C^f_T)_{x_T}$. Inverting the resulting isomorphism gives the displayed assertion of the item. The same simultaneous cone construction on the pasted comparisons gives its further-base-change compatibility; no properness of $h$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change; Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian. Application: Orgogozo, Lemma 4.2 proof, printed p. 12, and identity case at beginning of section 4, printed p. 11 (author PDF read online; archival PDF WANTED).

proof.text:
For the identity morphism of an arbitrary scheme $S$, define
$$\theta_S:p_2^*\underline M\longrightarrow R\Psi_{1_S}\underline M$$
as the adjoint of $\psi_{1_S}^*p_2^*\underline M=\underline M\xrightarrow{1}\underline M$; this uses $p_2\psi_{1_S}=1_S$. At a vanishing-topos point $(a,b\to a)$, the oriented-point cohomology formula, applied to $X=Y=S$ and both maps the identity, identifies its target with
$$R\Gamma(S_{(a)}\times_{S_{(a)}}S_{(b)},\underline M)=R\Gamma(S_{(b)},\underline M).$$
Its source stalk is $M$, and the map sends $m$ to the corresponding constant section. The strict-local ring is strictly henselian. The germ isomorphism and the constant-sheaf stalk formula identify its degree-zero sections with $M$; all positive cohomology vanishes by strictly henselian etale acyclicity. These assertions also hold with $\Lambda$-module coefficients: the germ isomorphism is $\Lambda$-linear, and identifies module sections with the exact module stalk functor, so its positive derived functors vanish. Thus $\theta_S$ is an isomorphism at every oriented point, and conservativity of those points makes it an isomorphism on the vanishing topos. Its inverse is the claimed $R\Psi_{1_S}\underline M\simeq p_2^*\underline M$.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change; Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian. Application: Orgogozo, Lemma 4.2 proof, printed p. 12, and identity case at beginning of section 4, printed p. 11 (author PDF read online; archival PDF WANTED).

proof.text:
For any $q:T\to S$ let $v:V_{1_T}\to V_{1_S}$ be the induced morphism. There is a canonical identification $v^*p_{2,S}^*\underline M=p_{2,T}^*\underline M$, since $p_{2,S}v=q p_{2,T}$ and pullback preserves constants. Under it,
$$\beta_q\circ v^*\theta_S=\theta_T.$$
Indeed transposition under $\psi_{1_T}^*\dashv R\Psi_{1_T}$ takes the left side to the pullback of $\varepsilon_S\circ\psi_{1_S}^*\theta_S=1_{\underline M}$; this equality is the defining adjunction equation for $\theta_S$. The right side has precisely the same adjunct $1_{\underline M}$. Uniqueness in the adjunction proves the equality. Both $\theta$ maps are invertible by step 5, hence so is $\beta_q$. This proves $\Psi$-goodness for the identity over every scheme. For $T'\to T\to S$, applying this same equality twice gives the composite $\theta_{T'}\,(v_{T'/T}^*v_{T/S}^*\theta_S)^{-1}$, which is also the expression for the composite base change by mate pasting. Thus the identity isomorphism has the asserted compatibility with arbitrary and iterated base changes.
